newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN GOVT URGED TO COME CLEAN ON AIDS PLAY.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN GOVT URGED TO COME CLEAN ON AIDS PLAY.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela's government would be "haunted" by its ill-fated AIDS musical unless it made public all details surrounding it, ousted deputy tourism minister Bantu Holomisa said on Monday.

"We need to clear this Sarafina issue once and for all and carry on building government...the more we are secretive about it the more it will haunt us for many more years to come," he said in an address to students at the University of Cape Town.

The health ministry initially said the $3 million musical Sarafina II aimed at building AIDS awareness would be paid for by the European Union, but this was repudiated by the EU which accused it of using the funds in violation of agreed procedures.
The EU also demanded that 10.5 million of the 14.2 million rand spent on the project had to be returned to the Department of Health for approved AIDS education.

An anonymous donor then offered to bail out the health ministry but withdrew last week, citing sustained pressure by opposition parties in parliament and newspapers to reveal his identity. South African taxpayers will now foot the bill.

Holomisa was sacked as deputy minister and expelled from the ruling African National Congress (ANC) after he questioned party ethics and accused an ANC cabinet minister of accepting a cash bribe. He has appealed against his expulsion.
